s: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act was passed in :
x: The Indian Parliament passed the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (NREGA) on 23 August, 2005. The Act was notified on 7 September, 2005 and came into force on 2 February, 2006 in 200 backward districts. On 2 October, 2009 an amendment was made in the National Rural Employment Guarantee Act 2005, to change the nomenclature of the Act from NREGA to Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA). MGNREGA was implemented in 200 districts in the first phase with effect from February, 2006 and extended subsequently, to additional 113 and 17 districts (total 330 districts) w.e.f. April 1, 2007 and May 15, 2007, respectively. The remaining districts were included under the Act w.e.f. April 1, 2008. The Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) or VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 was enacted by the Parliament in December, 2025 to replace MGNREGA. The VB-G RAM G Act, 2025 represents a comprehensive statutory overhaul of MGNREGA, aligning rural employment with the long-term vision of Viksit Bharat 2047, while strengthening accountability, infrastructure outcomes and income security. The Act modernizes the rural wage scheme by increasing guaranteed employment to 125 days per household and linking work with durable rural infrastructure.
